nodes.content: Enable mobile manipulators to distinguish object slip from localization drift while maintaining contact during furniture repositioning.
requirements: Reposition unseen furniture within 5 cm in 90% of trials with intermittent visual occlusion.
Identify slip versus localization drift with 90% balanced accuracy without external tracking during execution.

nodes.content: Fuse tactile shear, wheel odometry, and intermittent RGB-D in a contact-constrained estimator distinguishing slip from drift for furniture control.
Which tactile–odometric residuals distinguish gripper–furniture slip from map-frame localization drift during five-second RGB-D occlusions?
During five-second RGB-D occlusions, shear transients indicate slip; shear-stable wheel–contact residuals indicate drift, yielding ≥90% balanced accuracy.
Label slip/drift with training-only motion capture; train a shear–odometry classifier; evaluate unseen furniture through five-second occlusions without external tracking.
Run 120 OccludedFurniture trials on unseen furniture with induced slip or localization drift; ablate shear and score five-second-occlusion balanced accuracy.
Across 120 OccludedFurniture trials, shear–odometry achieved 84% balanced accuracy during five-second occlusions, below the hypothesized 90%.
Latency-aligned shear–arm closure residuals plus wheel odometry distinguish slip from drift at ≥90% balanced accuracy during five-second occlusions.
Evaluate latency-aligned shear–arm closure residuals against unaligned shear–odometry on 120 held-out OccludedFurniture slip/drift trials without execution-time tracking.
On 120 held-out OccludedFurniture trials, latency-aligned residuals reached 92% balanced accuracy versus 84% unaligned during five-second occlusions.
Replace the 84%-accurate baseline with latency-aligned shear–arm closure residuals, which achieved 92% balanced accuracy.
Test selected estimator in 100 unseen-furniture repositionings with five-second occlusions and no execution tracking; score post-run 5-cm success.
OccludedFurniture-100 report contains trial logs, post-run position errors, and the 5-cm success rate for the selected estimator.
How can contact-constrained estimation bound furniture-pose error when RGB-D is occluded and wheel odometry accumulates drift?
Measure contact-constrained versus odometry-only pose error in 60 contact-maintained, five-second-occlusion pushes with 2-cm/s wheel bias, using evaluation-only motion capture.
Across 60 biased, five-second-occlusion pushes, contact constraints reduced median furniture-to-gripper pose error from 8.7 to 2.4 cm.
Audit contact-constrained RGB-D fusion on OccludedFurniture-100: quantify 95% furniture-pose bound coverage during five-second occlusions, stratified by slip/drift.
OccludedFurniture-100 achieved 84/100 within-5-cm repositionings, below the 90% target; nominal 95% pose bounds covered 68% of slip intervals.
Reanalyze OccludedFurniture-100 logs to calibrate slip-conditioned pose bounds against post-run errors and identify occlusion-driven >5-cm misses.
OccludedFurniture-100: 11/16 >5-cm misses followed occluded slip; retrospective slip-conditioned bounds raised slip-interval coverage from 68% to 94%.
Retain contact constraints; pause for visual reacquisition when slip-conditioned pose bounds exceed 5 cm, targeting occluded-slip misses.
Use force-limited 1-cm contact micro-dithers to distinguish grip slip from map drift, then correct placement after RGB-D reacquisition.
Can force-limited, 1-cm contact micro-dithers distinguish grip slip from map drift during occlusion without breaking contact?
Slip induces >30-ms shear–arm phase lag during 1-cm micro-dithers; drift does not, enabling ≥90% balanced accuracy without contact loss.
Run 100 unseen-furniture pushes with force-limited 1-cm micro-dithers; score phase-lag accuracy, contact loss, and post-reacquisition 5-cm placement.
Across 100 unseen-furniture pushes, micro-dithers achieved 92% slip/drift balanced accuracy, 93% within-5-cm placement after reacquisition, and zero contact losses.
Adopt force-limited micro-dithers with visual reacquisition: 92% slip/drift balanced accuracy and 93% within-5-cm placement without contact loss.
Fuse wrist-mounted mmWave furniture range-rate with tactile shear to distinguish contact slip from map drift through RGB-D occlusions.
Can wrist mmWave range-rate separate grip slip from map drift despite self-motion and metal-leg multipath during five-second occlusions?
Ego-motion-compensated mmWave range-rate plus shear distinguishes slip from drift at ≥90% balanced accuracy despite metal-leg multipath during five-second occlusions.
Run 120 occluded pushes across metal-legged and wooden furniture; compare compensated mmWave–shear classification with shear-only using evaluation-only ground truth.
Across 120 occluded pushes, compensated mmWave–shear achieved 78% balanced accuracy on metal-legged furniture versus 92% on wood.
Gating multipath-inconsistent mmWave returns and falling back to shear–arm closure residuals should achieve ≥90% balanced accuracy on metal-legged furniture.
Test gated mmWave–shear fusion against ungated and closure-only baselines on 120 held-out metal/wood pushes; score balanced accuracy and 5-cm placement.
On 120 held-out pushes, gated fusion achieved 92% metal-leg balanced accuracy and 91% within-5-cm placement; ungated achieved 77% accuracy.
Stress-test gated fusion on 80 unseen chrome-legged furniture pushes with five-second occlusions; log multipath rejection and slip/drift balanced accuracy.
On 80 unseen chrome-legged pushes, gated fusion reached 84% balanced accuracy; coherent multipath evaded rejection during five-second occlusions.
Two-angle radar beam steering rejects coherent multipath; shear–arm closure fallback yields ≥90% slip/drift balanced accuracy on unseen chrome-legged furniture.
Run 100 held-out chrome-legged pushes with five-second occlusions; compare two-angle steering plus fallback against single-angle gating for balanced accuracy.
On 100 held-out chrome-legged pushes, two-angle steering plus fallback reached 91% slip/drift balanced accuracy versus 83% single-angle gating.
Test validated two-angle fusion on 100 unseen chrome-legged pushes under five-second occlusions; score balanced accuracy and 5-cm placement.
On 100 unseen chrome-legged pushes, two-angle fusion achieved 86% balanced accuracy and 88% within-5-cm placement; specular returns persisted.
Polarization-diverse radar flags persistent specular returns; shear–arm closure fallback yields ≥90% slip/drift balanced accuracy on unseen chrome-legged furniture.
Compare polarization-diverse rejection against two-angle steering, both with shear–arm fallback, across 120 unseen chrome-legged pushes; score five-second-occlusion balanced accuracy.
On 120 unseen chrome-legged pushes, two-angle fusion achieved 91% balanced accuracy versus 86% for polarization-diverse fusion.
Stress-test polarization-diverse radar on 80 unseen chrome-legged pushes during five-second occlusions; measure specular-return recall and fallback slip/drift balanced accuracy.
On 80 unseen chrome-legged pushes, polarization-diverse fallback achieved 91% balanced accuracy and 94% specular-return recall during five-second occlusions.
Retain both radar variants for cross-cohort validation: two-angle outperformed polarization head-to-head, but polarization reached 91% in a separate cohort.
Combine onboard lidar wall anchors with gripper–furniture kinematics in a factor graph to detect slip and correct placement during occlusions.
Do lidar wall-anchor residuals remain independent of gripper slip when furniture occludes most room geometry?
With ≥20% visible wall returns, anchor residuals track localization drift independently of gripper slip, enabling ≥90% balanced accuracy.
Collect wall-visibility-stratified pushes; fit lidar-anchor and contact factors; compare slip/drift accuracy and placement under five-second RGB-D occlusions.
Run 120 occluded unseen-furniture pushes stratified by ≥20% versus <20% wall returns; measure anchor–slip residual correlation and balanced accuracy.
In 60 pushes with ≥20% wall returns, anchor–slip residual correlation was 0.07; slip/drift balanced accuracy reached 92%.
Apply anchor factors validated at ≥20% wall visibility to 60 low-visibility pushes; measure slip/drift balanced accuracy and 5-cm placement.
WallAnchor-LowVis report contains per-trial wall-return fractions, anchor residuals, slip/drift predictions, and post-run placement errors for 60 pushes.
Audit WallAnchor-LowVis report for missing records and residual-label consistency; compute low-visibility balanced accuracy and within-5-cm placement.
All 60 low-visibility records passed audit; lidar–contact fusion achieved 92% slip/drift balanced accuracy and 55/60 within-5-cm placements.
Fuse contact-wrench change points with ceiling-feature visual odometry, rejecting slip-corrupted contact factors while correcting base drift during furniture pushes.
Can ceiling-feature odometry distinguish base drift from grip slip when lighting changes coincide with contact-wrench transients?
Photometrically normalized ceiling odometry plus wrench change points yields ≥90% slip/drift balanced accuracy under alternating overhead lighting.
Run 120 unseen-furniture pushes with synchronized lighting switches and induced slip/drift; compare normalized ceiling odometry against raw using balanced accuracy.
Across 120 lighting-switch pushes, normalized ceiling odometry reached 82% balanced accuracy versus 76% raw; switching shadows mimicked drift.
Run 80 paired pushes with lighting switches coincident versus staggered 2 s from wrench transients; compare normalized-odometry balanced accuracy.
In 80 paired pushes, normalized ceiling–wrench fusion achieved 92% balanced accuracy with staggered lighting, versus 78% coincident.
Gate shadow-contaminated ceiling features for 300 ms, bridging with inertial odometry, to achieve ≥90% slip/drift balanced accuracy under coincident switches.
Compare 300-ms shadow gating plus inertial bridging against normalized ceiling–wrench fusion on 100 held-out coincident-switch pushes; score balanced accuracy.
On 100 held-out coincident-switch pushes, shadow gating plus inertial bridging reached 91% balanced accuracy versus 79% ungated fusion.
Deploy validated shadow gating in 100 unseen-furniture repositionings with coincident lighting switches and five-second RGB-D occlusions; score accuracy and placement.
On 100 unseen-furniture repositionings, shadow gating achieved 86% balanced accuracy under coincident switches, below the hypothesized 90%.
Adaptive shadow gating until ceiling-inlier recovery, with inertial bridging, restores ≥90% balanced accuracy under coincident lighting switches.
Using n70 failure logs, compare inlier-recovery gating with fixed 300-ms gating on 100 new coincident-switch pushes; score balanced accuracy.
On 100 new coincident-switch pushes, inlier-recovery gating reached 87% balanced accuracy versus 85% fixed gating, below 90%.
Stratify 120 held-out coincident-switch pushes by ceiling-inlier recovery delay; measure adaptive-gating slip/drift accuracy for ≤500-ms versus >500-ms delays.
Across 120 held-out pushes, adaptive gating reached 94% balanced accuracy for ≤500-ms inlier recovery versus 80% for slower recovery.
Trigger force-limited micro-dithers when ceiling-inlier recovery exceeds 500 ms; combined classification reaches ≥90% balanced accuracy under coincident switches.
Using failed adaptive-gating baseline and recovery-delay stratification, compare >500-ms-triggered micro-dithers against adaptive gating on 100 coincident-switch pushes; score balanced accuracy.
On 100 coincident-switch pushes, recovery-triggered micro-dithers reached 92% slip/drift balanced accuracy versus 86% adaptive gating alone.
Use adaptive ceiling gating for ≤500-ms recovery; otherwise trigger micro-dithers, raising coincident-switch balanced accuracy to 92%.
Validate selected gating/micro-dither policy on 100 unseen-furniture moves with coincident lighting switches; score occluded balanced accuracy and 5-cm placement.
Execute 100 unseen-furniture moves using selected gating/micro-dither policy through five-second occlusions; measure slip/drift accuracy and post-run 5-cm success.
GatedDither-100 report contains per-trial slip/drift predictions, post-run placement errors, occlusion intervals, and contact-loss flags for 100 moves.
